vehicle_type.intro:
Please first put the boat on its stand (or tied up in the water) with the propeller(s) clear of hands and lines.

Then choose your **frame class** and select everything **that is true for your vehicle**.

All following steps depend on these answers.

steering_output.intro: Choose the **steering type**; for a rudder or a steered motor, assign the steering servo output and confirm its direction.
steering_output.help:
**Steering type**

* **Rudder or steered motor**: a servo moves a rudder (or turns an outboard / jet nozzle), and one throttle output drives the motor.
* **Two motors (differential thrust)**: a left and a right motor steer by running at different speeds. There is no steering servo, so this step only asks for the type.

**Vectored thrust**: when the servo turns the motor itself, enter the motor's angle at full steering - ArduPilot then steers by the thrust direction, much better at low speed.

The flight controller needs to know which SERVO/MAIN output drives the steering servo; a change of output channel needs a **reboot** (offered at the end of Phase 1); the wizard writes `SERVOx_FUNCTION=26` for you and clears it from any other output.

Keep hands clear of the rudder before testing. *Test L*/*Test R* hold the steering stick left/right by the *test deflection* for a few seconds - the vehicle stays disarmed, since Rover moves the steering servo while disarmed. The *+*/*-* buttons next to MIN/MAX/TRIM change the value immediately and move the servo to it the same way. If it moves the wrong way, check **Reverse output**.

MIN/MAX/TRIM set the servo's mechanical end stops and the position that holds a straight course.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>

motor_output.intro: Choose the motor driver signal, assign the throttle/motor output(s), confirm their direction, and find the throttle dead-zone - with the boat **in the water, tied up**.
motor_output.help:
**Motor driver / ESC signal** (MOT_PWM_TYPE): *Normal* for hobby ESCs and servos, *Brushed* types for H-bridge motor drivers (then also set the PWM frequency), *DShot* for DShot ESCs. A change needs a **reboot**.

The flight controller needs to know which SERVO/MAIN output(s) drive the motor(s); the wizard writes `SERVOx_FUNCTION` for you (70 throttle, or 73/74 left/right for two motors) and clears it from any other output.

**Put the boat in the water and tie it up** before running a motor: many boat motors and ESCs are water-cooled and overheat when run dry, and a free-spinning propeller is dangerous. *Test ↑*/*Test ↓* run the motor briefly forward/reverse with ArduPilot's motor test. Note: the motor test **arms the vehicle** for its duration and disarms it afterwards; it needs calibrated RC, the safety switch pressed and passing arming checks. Start it disarmed. If a propeller pushes the wrong way, check **Reverse output**. Thrusters for boats and submarines (e.g. Blue Robotics) work with normal reversible ESCs; for twin motors use clockwise and counter-clockwise propellers.

**Dead-zone**: motors often need some power before they move. *Probe* next to *Minimum throttle* ramps the power; press Continue when the propeller starts turning - the value is proposed as **MOT_THR_MIN** (press Apply to keep it).

MOT_THR_MAX limits full power, MOT_SLEWRATE limits how fast throttle may change (%/s), MOT_STR_THR_MIX (two motors only) sets how much of the throttle range steering may use.

A change of output channel needs a **reboot** (offered at the end of Phase 1).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>

accel.help:
**Gyro**: keep the vehicle still. **Level**: sets the 'flat' reference (AHRS trim) - do it with the boat level as it floats (on its stand, waterline level). **6-position accel calibration**: the flight controller asks for LEVEL, LEFT, RIGHT, NOSE DOWN, NOSE UP and BACK; place the vehicle accordingly and press Continue each time. Do the 6-position calibration once per vehicle, level calibration whenever the mounting changed.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/FilterReview> and <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/FilterTool> to review/configure gyro noise filter settings in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-accelerometer-calibration.html>

compass.help:
The onboard calibration runs on the flight controller. Hold the vehicle in the air (it is small enough) and rotate it so every side points to the ground. Keep it away from metal, speakers, motors and cables with high current. **Fitness** (lower is better; values up to about 10-15 are fine). *External compass orientation* must match how the external compass module is mounted (if any). Auto declination uses the GPS position for the local magnetic declination.

**Large Vehicle MagCal** (shown because you checked *too heavy to rotate* on the Frame step): instead of rotating the vehicle, park it still and enter its current heading relative to **true north** (e.g. read from a phone compass app in true-north mode, or a known landmark bearing). ArduPilot computes the calibration in one shot from the World Magnetic Model at the vehicle's GPS location - needs a 3D GPS fix.

**Orientation of an external compass**: the rotate-by-hand calibration detects it by itself (*Detect orientation during calibration*). Large Vehicle MagCal can't - it needs the orientation set first: **Probe** next to *External compass orientation* finds it from two headings (front to magnetic north, then south; needs two reboots).

**Motor interference compensation** (shown when the battery monitor reports a current - set it up on the *Battery monitor* step just before, and reboot after changing the monitor type): current in the motors, ESC and power wires adds its own magnetic field, so the heading drifts while driving. *Measure compass-motor interference* runs the motors with the boat tied up in the water and measures how much the compass reading changes per amp; ArduPilot then subtracts that (COMPASS_MOTCT = *Use current*). Do it after the compass calibration, and again after moving the compass or re-routing power wires.

**Compasses found / Use compass n**: every compass the flight controller detected, internal or external, and the order ArduPilot uses them in. On a boat the internal compass sits close to motors and power wires; if an external compass is fitted, setting the internal one to *Not used* usually gives a steadier heading. At least one compass must stay in use. (ArduPilot switches compasses by their priority - COMPASS_USE / USE2 / USE3 follow COMPASS_PRIO1..3_ID, not the detection order; the wizard picks the right one.)

**Declination** (shown without a GPS, or with *Automatic declination* off): the angle between true and magnetic north where you drive, east positive. ArduPilot can only look it up from its position; without one it uses this value - leaving it at 0 turns every heading by the local declination.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/MAGFit> to calibrate the compass from flight logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-calibration-in-mission-planner.html>

predrive.intro: Check GPS/EKF/RC/battery and enter the free space around the vehicle's START position. ARM the boat on the water before continuing.
predrive.help:
**Everything from here on drives the vehicle.** Choose open water without boats, swimmers or lines nearby, preferably with little wind and current, put the boat in, and **arm** it with the Arm button (or your transmitter).

**Where the distances are measured from:** every automatic run starts where the vehicle stands at that moment (its *start point*), and the distances below are measured from there:

* **Straight runway** - the free distance straight ahead of the vehicle's nose. Straight runs go forward only.
* **Circle** - all automatic turns go to the **right**. The free circle lies beside the vehicle: the vehicle stands on its edge, facing along it, with the circle's centre to its right (half the diameter away).

```
     .-~~~~~-.
   /           \
  ^      +      |
   \           /
     '-.___.-'

^ vehicle on the edge, facing up
+ centre, half the diameter to its right
```

Wind and current carry the boat between runs: bring it back to a start point with enough free water before each one. The automatic stop measures the straight-line distance from the start point (from GPS/EKF position) and ends the run at the limit. It can't tell a planned circle from a drift sideways, so the circle is the area to keep clear, not a fence. Put the vehicle back at a start point with enough free space before each run.

It uses RC override in Manual mode (open-loop tests) and Guided mode (closed-loop tests); if the wizard or the link dies, the override expires after ~3 s and the transmitter/failsafe takes over. The **STOP** button releases all commands, switches to Hold and disarms.

The RC failsafe test verifies that switching the transmitter off really stops the vehicle.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>

direction_check.help:
The boat moves slowly forward and then steers right. The wizard compares the commanded direction with the measured speed and yaw rate. If something is inverted it offers to fix it (toggle *reversed* on the motor/steering output, or swap left/right on twin-motor boats).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>

top_speed.help:
**SPEED_MAX** is the speed at full throttle - the vehicle accelerates in a straight line at 100% throttle until the speed is constant. From the same run the maximum **acceleration** (ATC_ACCEL_MAX) and **deceleration** (ATC_DECEL_MAX, 0 = same as acceleration) are derived with a safety factor of 0.9. Wind and current add to or take from the speed: measure in calm conditions, or run once each way and use the lower result. If the free water ahead is too short the speed is still rising: the result is only a lower bound - repeat with more free water.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-throttle-and-speed.html>

turning.help:
**Radius**: drives a full-lock circle at low speed and computes radius = speed / yaw rate. **Max turn rate**: the peak yaw rate with full steering (turning on the spot for two motors, medium speed with a rudder). It is multiplied by 0.9 and written to **ACRO_TURN_RATE** and **ATC_STR_RAT_MAX**; the steepest yaw-rate slope gives **ATC_STR_ACC_MAX**. Twin-motor boats can turn on the spot: also review the pivot parameters in the *Navigation* step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-steering-rate.html>

gains.help:
Uses the same maths as ArduPilot's **QuickTune** script: *steering FF* = steering output / measured yaw rate; *speed*: CRUISE_SPEED and CRUISE_THROTTLE are the steady speed and throttle at a medium throttle level, and the speed P and I start at throttle-per-(m/s). Steering P = I = 0.5 x FF. Filters are set to half the gyro filter. Run these tests in calm water, with little wind and current. Optionally assign a transmitter switch to ArduPilot's **QuickTune** script for later fine-tuning while driving (see the switch field's ❓; scripting itself is enabled on the **Scripting** step).

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/PIDReview> to review PID tune from logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-process.html>

verify.help:
In Guided mode the vehicle follows a **speed step** and a **yaw-rate step**. Overshoot, rise time and steady-state error are measured; P and I are corrected (overshoot -> lower P/I, slow -> raise P, steady error -> raise I) and the test is repeated up to the chosen number of rounds. In *manual* mode you drive in Acro and get achieved/desired ratios (edit the values yourself). The boat needs a position estimate (GPS) for Guided mode.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/PIDReview> to review PID tune from logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-process.html>

final.help:
Review the list of changed parameters, save a parameter backup (**Ctrl+P**, **Backup**) and keep the file somewhere safe as the record of the finished setup. **Next steps**: run a small Auto mission square, watch the tracking in your ground station, and lower WP_SPEED / raise NAVL1_PERIOD if the vehicle oscillates. Check that the boat holds its position in Loiter. Re-run *Verify* after changing the propeller, payload or battery.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/apmrover-setup.html>

ekf_sources.help:
ArduPilot's EKF (EKF3) estimates where the vehicle is, how fast it moves and where it points, from the sources chosen here. The default (source set 1): horizontal position and velocity from GPS, vertical position from the barometer, vertical velocity from GPS, heading from the compass - right for a vehicle with GPS and compass.

**Heading from**: *Compass* is the default. Without a compass choose the *GSF estimator* (it works out the heading from GPS velocity and the IMU once the vehicle drives); with a dual-antenna (moving baseline) GPS choose *GPS, compass as fallback* (or *GPS*). The wizard proposes these when they fit.

**Vertical position from**: *GPS* instead of the barometer is an option with an accurate (RTK) GPS; a rover rarely needs altitude, but it is logged and shown.

Without GPS: *Beacon* or *ExternalNav* (visual odometry) for position, *ExternalNav* for velocity (optical flow needs ground texture and doesn't work over water).

**Source sets**: up to three sets (EK3_SRC1_* to EK3_SRC3_*) - e.g. set 1 GPS for outdoors, set 2 beacons or visual odometry for indoors. Pick a set to configure it. An RC switch changes between them in operation, or *Use this source set now* switches immediately (apply first). Source changes need a **reboot**.

**Estimator**: standard firmware since 4.5 only contains EKF3 (EKF2 is compiled out and will be removed), so it must be selected and enabled. The EKF runs one instance per IMU ticked here.

**Sensor settings** (shown for the sensors the vehicle has): how much the EKF trusts visual odometry, and the measurement delays of optical flow and beacons.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-ekf-sources.html>

fields.steering_output.rev_steering:
Use *Test L* / *Test R* above: if the rudder (or the steered motor) turns the boat the other way, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.min_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse at full **left** rudder: as far as it goes without binding. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (boat disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.max_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse at full **right** rudder: as far as it goes without binding. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (boat disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.trim_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse that holds a straight course. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (boat disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_throttle:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the motor pushes the boat backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_left:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the LEFT motor pushes the boat backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_right:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the RIGHT motor pushes the boat backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.compass.compassmot_power:
Highest motor power during the measurement. The motors run at a third, two thirds and all of it, each for about 4.5 s with motor-off pauses in between. More power means more current and a more reliable result - use as much as is safe with the boat tied up.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.predrive.runway:
The free water **straight ahead of the vehicle's nose**, measured from where it stands when a run starts. Straight runs use part of it and stop automatically once the vehicle is that far from its start point: the direction check at most 20 % (at least 3 m), top speed and cruise runs at most 60 % (the rest is for stopping), the speed-controller step up to 90 %.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_rpm:
Engine or propeller RPM from a hall-effect/optical sensor, or motor RPM from ESC telemetry.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rpm.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_optical_flow:
A downward camera measuring ground speed - for navigation without GPS. It doesn't work over water: the camera needs ground texture.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-optical-flow-sensors-landingpage.html>

actions.predrive.Test RC failsafe:
Checks the radio failsafe while armed. ArduPilot's failsafe does nothing (and reports nothing) in **Hold** or **RTL** - unless `FS_OPTIONS` bit 0 is set - so if the vehicle is in one of them, the test first asks to switch to **Manual** (keep the throttle stick centred). Then: keep the boat tied up or drifting slowly, switch the **transmitter off**, wait about 3 s and press Continue - the log shows whether the flight controller reported the failsafe and which mode it switched to. Switch the transmitter back on and press Continue - the log shows whether the failsafe was reported as **cleared**. If not, another failsafe is still active (e.g. GCS or battery). The vehicle stays in the failsafe's mode (usually Hold): switch the mode with your transmitter before driving.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-failsafes.html>
actions.compass.Measure compass-motor interferen:
Runs the motor(s) with ArduPilot's motor test at increasing power (skid steering: left, then right), with the boat tied up in the water, and records battery current and compass field. The field change per amp, negated, is proposed as the compensation; Apply writes it. Needs a battery monitor that measures current. The log shows every power level and how strong the interference is.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
actions.accel.Level calibration:
Tells ArduPilot that the vehicle's current attitude is *level*: put the boat level as it floats (on its stand, waterline level) and keep it still, then press Continue. ArduPilot stores the small remaining tilt as trim. Do the 6-position calibration first.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-accelerometer-calibration.html>
actions.direction_check.Run direction check:
Checks that *forward* drives forward and *right* steers right. Automatic: the boat moves slowly forward for about 1.5 s, then drives a gentle right turn for about 2 s (stops after a few metres at most); manual: you drive forward and then steer right. If a direction is wrong, it offers the fix (reverse the motor or steering output, or swap the left/right motors) and asks before changing anything. Repeat after a fix. Before the vehicle moves, a safety prompt explains what will happen; press Continue to start. Keep the transmitter in hand (switch to Hold/Manual to take over) - **STOP** switches to Hold and disarms at once.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>

probes.motor_output.MOT_THR_MIN:
━━ Minimum throttle probe ━━
What happens: ArduPilot's motor test drives the throttle motor (skid steering: the LEFT motor) with 1 % power, then 2 %, 3 % ... - one step every 2 seconds, up to 40 %. MOT_THR_MIN is 0 during the ramp and restored afterwards. The power one step below the moment you press Continue is proposed as MOT_THR_MIN; it is written only when you press Apply.

Your tasks:
  1. Put the boat in the water and tie it up, and connect the battery so the ESC is powered.
  2. Confirm the start below, then watch the propeller (or the water behind it) closely.
  3. Press Continue the moment the propeller starts to turn. Cancel stops the ramp without a result.

Take care:
  • Boat in the water and tied up: the motor test drives the motor although the vehicle is disarmed (ArduPilot arms for the test).
  • Keep hands, lines and loose clothing away from the propeller - don't run a water-cooled motor or ESC dry.
  • React promptly: the probe already takes one step back for a short delay; every further 2 s of delay adds 1 % to the result.
  • Wait for the propeller itself to turn - a brushed motor may hum before it starts.
  • The log shows each power step and the pulse width sent to the ESC.
probes.compass.Measure compass-motor interferen:
━━ Compass-motor interference measurement ━━
What happens: ArduPilot's motor test runs the driving motor (skid steering: the LEFT, then the RIGHT motor) at a third, two thirds and all of the motor power set above - each level about 4.5 s, with the motor off in between. Meanwhile the wizard records the battery current and the compass field. Motor interference compensation is off during the run and set back afterwards. About 30 s per motor. The result is only proposed; Apply writes it.

Your tasks:
  1. Put the boat in the water and tie it up, and power it from its battery (the current sensor must see the motor current).
  2. Put it where it will stay during the whole run, away from metal, and keep magnets and tools away.
  3. Confirm the start below, then stand back and wait for the result.

Take care:
  • Boat tied up in the water: the motor test drives the motors although the vehicle is disarmed (ArduPilot arms for the test).
  • Keep hands, lines and loose clothing away from the propellers; check the lines hold.
  • Keep the boat from swinging round at its lines, and don't move or anything magnetic near it while it measures - that would look like interference.
  • Cancel or STOP ends the run at once; nothing is changed then.
probes.orientation.AHRS_ORIENTATION:
━━ Board orientation probe ━━
What happens: AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to None and the flight controller reboots, so the accelerometer reports in the board's own axes. The probe then measures the direction of gravity in two poses and picks the mounting that fits both. At the end it asks whether to apply the result and reboots once more - about a minute in total. The vehicle stays disarmed.

Your tasks:
  1. After the first reboot: put the boat LEVEL as it floats (on its stand, waterline level), keep it still and press Continue. It measures for about 2 s.
  2. Then tilt it so its NOSE (front) points straight DOWN - pitch it forward by about 90 deg, without rolling it to the side - hold it still and press Continue.
  3. Check the detected orientation: Continue applies it, Cancel discards it.

Take care:
  • Keep the vehicle completely still while it measures (motors off); resting it against something is better than holding it in the air.
  • 'Nose' means the vehicle's front, not the arrow on the flight controller - finding that difference is the point of the probe.
  • It needn't be exact: the probe picks the closest of ArduPilot's mounting options and tells you how sure it is.
  • Secure loose parts (battery, wires) before tilting, and don't pull the USB / telemetry cable out; after each reboot the wizard reconnects by itself.
  • Cancel at any time restores the original orientation (with a reboot).
  • A changed orientation invalidates earlier accelerometer and compass calibrations - the Accelerometer and Compass steps calibrate them afterwards.

prompts.drive.must_be_armed: The boat must be ARMED for this action (use the Arm button, on the water).
prompts.drive.arm_confirm: ARM the boat? In the water, area clear, nobody near the propellers.
prompts.predrive.not_armed: boat is disarmed - use the Arm button (in the water, area clear)
prompts.predrive.rc_failsafe_start: Boat tied up or drifting slowly. Switch your TRANSMITTER OFF, wait ~3 s, then press Continue.
prompts.compass.compassmot_start: Boat in the water and tied up, battery connected? Start the compass-motor measurement?
prompts.compass.compassmot_load_note: (tied up, the propeller is loaded much as when underway).
prompts.accel.level_position: Put the boat LEVEL as it floats (on its stand, waterline level), keep it still.
prompts.motor_output.ramp_start: Boat in the water and tied up, propeller clear? Start the motor ramp?
prompts.motor_output.ramp_watch: Watch the propeller: press Continue the moment it starts to turn.
prompts.motor_output.ramp_found: Propeller started to turn at about {percent}% -> suggested MOT_THR_MIN = {percent}
prompts.servo_outputs.motor_test_warning: arms the boat for the test - in the water and tied up, propeller clear!
